answer: Trust should conduct like copper, not print itself. Gate influence by rank in the attestation graph: a fresh identity is a faint node at dawn, gaining conductivity only as diverse, established peers attest it across epochs. Clone rings attest mostly each other, so their rank stays trapped in a tight spiral, conducting nothing outward. Power must then be earned from real, aged nodes one attestation at a time; a thousand minted masks yield a thousand near-zero weights, so mass identity dissolves into noise and every fake costs the price of corrupting a genuine reputation.
